To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of endotoxemia against background of hyperthyroidsism is characterized by more pronounced kidney involvement, which is associated with increased apoptosis of nephrocytes in the proximal tubule.
chronic endotoxemic nephrotoxicity is more pronounced in hyperthyroidism.

the kidneys of rats with chronic endotoxemic nephropathy against the background of experimental hyperthyroidism were characterized by pronounced glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis with a significant increase in the number of apoptotic nephrocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of nephrotoxic lesions in the course of chronic endotoxinemia and hyperthyroidism and their possible pathogenetic links.
the study of morphological and immunohistochemical characteristics of kidneys in chronic endotoxemic conditions against the background of thyrotoxicosis.
the study of the effects of endotoxemia on the morphofunctional characteristics of the kidneys in rats with hyperfunctioning thyroid gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kidney is a target organ of chronic endotoxinemia, which can lead to nephropathy and renal insufficiency.
the development of chronic endotoxin-induced renal damage in rats is accompanied by increased expression of proapoptotic markers.
thyroid hormone excess in combination with chronic endotoxemic stress causes more pronounced nephropathy and renal failure than in the case of endotoxemia alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of chronic endotoxinemia against the background of thyroid hormone excess causes more pronounced nephropathy and renal failure.
chronic endotoxemic stress against the background of thyroid hyperfunction is accompanied by a more pronounced development of renal pathology.
the development of hyperthyroid nephropathy is associated with the formation of a number of morphofunctional disorders of the kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of chronic kidney disease is associated with increased expression of apoptosis markers and the severity of renal damage is higher in animals with hyperthyroid endotoxemia.
the development of nephrotoxicity in hyperthyroidism is associated with the formation of oxidative stress and the development of apoptosis.
the development of chronic kidney disease in hyperthyroidism is associated with the activation of apoptotic processes in the proximal tubular epithelial cells.
